## The miss

This round dispatched three cards at once on surfaces I checked against all 16 open PRs and reported **CLEAR**:

| card | declared surface |
|---|---|
| objectui#8071 slice 13 | `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` + `packages/plugin-grid/src/**` |
| objectui#9779 | `packages/plugin-form/src/**` |
| objectui#9794 | `scripts/changeset-polarity-census.mjs` + its pin |

⛔ **objectui#9779's PR objectui#9833 touches the parity file** (+1/−1) — slice 13's surface. Measured on its file list, ⛔ not inferred.

## Why the check could not have caught it, and what would have

⭐ My serial check enumerates **open PRs**. Both of these PRs were **created after** that check ran, by devs I had just dispatched. ⇒ the instrument was looking at the right thing and could not see the thing that mattered: ⛔ **an open-PR scan does not cover work I am about to create.**

The gap is in how I derived objectui#9779's surface. I took it from the card's subject — a renderer defect in `packages/plugin-form` — and ⛔ did not ask what else a **pinned** behaviour's repair must touch. The `object-form.sections` entry in `MEMBER_PINS` carries prose **describing the behaviour being repaired**, and that prose lives in the parity file. ⇒ any card whose behaviour objectui#8071 has pinned inherits the ledger as part of its surface.

⭐ **The rule this seat should have applied, stated so it is checkable:** before declaring surfaces disjoint, intersect each card's surface with **the surfaces of the cards being dispatched in the same round**, ⛔ not only with open PRs — and for any card whose behaviour is pinned, add the ledger file to its surface.

## Disposition — ⛔ neither dev is at fault and neither is being sent back

objectui#9833's parity-file edit is **correct and owed**: it repairs a registered sentence that described the pre-fix behaviour. ⛔ Reverting it would leave the ledger asserting something the renderer no longer does.

slice 13's branch was still at its base commit when this was found, so nothing has conflicted. Its dev has been told: keep working; immediately before pushing, re-read `origin/main` and merge if objectui#9833 has landed — ⛔ never reverting that one-line repair while resolving — and otherwise push and let this seat take the conflict at enqueue time.

⚠️ And a consequence worth naming: **a ledger count taken before a mid-flight merge must not be carried across it.** Slice 13 has been told to re-take its set-identity and ceiling readings after any merge and to report which ref each number came from.

Recorded on both cards rather than left in a subagent message, because a coordination fact that lives only in a dispatch channel does not exist.

**ACCEPT — PR objectui#9833.** Verified by the `domain:spec` @ objectui seat (session `session_01UanLVj6xvbS6puBCewLr8L`) on `origin/main` `26ac50369`.

Reading taken 2026-09-18T08:20Z.

## 1. ⛔ FIRST — the dev corrected this card, and the correction is mine to own

This card's table said **five** arms render `description`. ⭐ **Four do.** `drawer` also drops it — `ObjectForm`'s drawer map copies the key onto `DrawerForm`'s section config and `DrawerForm`'s **own** divider push never reads it, so it is lost one layer later. Measured through the real renderer by both routes.

⭐ That table was **wrong when it was written**, ⛔ not rotted — so it takes the **correction** repair, and I have corrected it in the card body just now, with the falsifier named and the reading pointed at objectui#9834. ⛔ Not dated, because dating preserves a truth that never existed.

⚠️ My own cross-check was **weaker than the dev's and I am not pretending otherwise**: I read the seven `type: 'section-divider'` push sites on `origin/main` with a line window, which corroborates `drawer` (both pushes carry no `description`) and the default arm (the defect), but ⛔ does not by itself settle `tabbed`/`wizard`. The dev drove the real renderer; that is the better instrument and I am not overturning it with a coarser one.

## 2. The fix

One key copied onto the divider row — `description: section.description` — in `SimpleObjectForm`'s grouped branch. ⛔ Nothing else in the renderer moved.

⭐ **And the `if (label)` gate was deliberately NOT widened**, with the reason written into the code beside it: that gate also carries the ADR-0089 `visibleWhen` predicate row, the objectui#6236 membership claim that gates the whole group, and the collapse pair whose *"an untitled bucket is never collapsible"* rule the gate is what implements.

## 3. The pin moved with the fix, in the same change

Row 6 is **rewritten** from *"`description` is DROPPED"* to *"`description` REACHES the divider"*, keeping the live control (the sibling `label` in the same call), and a **new row 7** pins the boundary that remains. The ledger's `pins` prose in `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` is updated in the same PR to say the key changed hands and that the boundary is pinned beside it.

⭐ The ablation deletes the one copied key and reddens **exactly** row 6 — *"expected [] to deeply equal [ Totals as invoiced ]"* — with row 7 and the other five staying green, restored with blob-hash equality and empty `git diff HEAD`. ⇒ ⛔ the pin was not weakened to get green, and ⛔ the fix did not land leaving it red. Both halves of what this dispatch demanded.

## 4. ⚠️ RULINGS on the two questions handed back

**Q1 — `Refs` or a closing keyword? → the closing keyword, and it is now on the PR.**

The card's repro, its table and its judgement are all about a **labelled** section, and all of that is discharged. The headingless shape is a new and separately-ruled question, now carded. I have upgraded the PR body myself and read it back.

⭐ **And the dev's reason for not taking it unilaterally is the part worth keeping:** *"a wrong closing keyword fails SILENTLY at merge time while a wrong `Refs` fails visibly."* ⇒ under uncertainty it chose the failure mode that announces itself. That is the right way to pick a default, and I would rather review a conservative `Refs` than discover a card closed that should not have been.

**Q2 — widen the `if (label)` gate? → NO. Option A confirmed, and it is not close.**

Widening it would newly let a headingless section's `visibleWhen` predicate gate its whole group, and newly let a declared `collapsed: true` on such a member take its fields out of the DOM. ⭐ **Those are rulings about `visibleWhen` and `collapsed`, ⛔ not about `description`.** A card repairing a blurb does not get to change two other keys' runtime semantics on the way past. The boundary is pinned as behaviour, so option B stays cheap to take later and is ⛔ not silently foreclosed — which is exactly what pinning is for.

## 5. Changeset

⭐ A real `patch`, ⛔ not an empty declaration — and **measured**: the compiled divider push in `dist/index.js` now carries `description: r.description` (the source spelling does not survive minification, so the compiled property is the marker), against a lit control present in four published artifacts, an absent control (the pin sentinel) nowhere in `dist`, and ⭐ **a second absent control inside the same artifact** — three structurally identical divider pushes that carry no `description` — proving the bundler is not inventing the key. `check:changeset-presence` was **red before the changeset and green after**, which is the instrument demonstrating it can fail.

## 6. Filed from this hand-back

- **objectui#9834** — the drawer arm drops the same key, one layer later, at `DrawerForm`'s own divider push. ⚠️ Its card notes that drawer's behaviour currently has **no member pin watching it**, so whoever fixes it must pin it too.
- **objectui#9835** — after this PR, a member with a `description` and neither `name` nor `label` still drops its blurb, because the divider is gated on a heading. Carries the three contracts hanging off that gate, so the direction is a decision-box question, ⛔ not an execution-seat call.

⚠️ And one observation I am recording rather than filing, because the dev is right that it has no owner: **the ledger's `pins` prose is never compared mechanically** — only the pin file's existence and whether it names the block and key are checked. ⇒ any entry can go on describing behaviour that has since changed, exactly as this one did until this PR corrected it. ⭐ That is a property of objectui#8068's gate design, and it is the reason the ledger touch in this PR mattered: nothing would have caught it.

## 7. Serial

⚠️ This PR touches `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` (+1/−1), which I had declared clear for objectui#8071 slice 13 in the same round. ⛔ That was my scoping miss, recorded on both cards; the edit here is **correct and owed**, and slice 13 has been told to merge rather than revert it.
